rows.stem:
Match the IUDs in Column I with suitable example in Column II.
| Column I | Column II |
|---|---|
| a. Non-medicated | i. Lippes loop |
| b. Copper releasing | ii. LNG-20 |
| c. Hormone releasing | iii. Multiload 375 |
rows.solution:
Intrauterine devices (IUDs) are inserted by doctors or expert nurses into the uterus through the vagina, and they come in three kinds:
- **Non-medicated IUDs**, for example the **Lippes loop**.
- **Copper releasing IUDs**, for example CuT, Cu7 and **Multiload 375**. The copper ions released suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms.
- **Hormone releasing IUDs**, for example Progestasert and **LNG-20**. They make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to the sperms.

So a matches i, b matches iii and c matches ii, and the answer is option (C) a-i, b-iii, c-ii.

rows.stem: If a genetic disease is transferred from a phenotypically normal but carrier female to only some of the male progeny, the disease is :
A doctor identifies symptoms of nasal congestion, headache, sore throat, hoarseness and cough in a patient. The conclusion is that the patient is infected by a pathogen :
rows.solution: Nasal congestion and discharge, sore throat, hoarseness, cough, headache and tiredness are the symptoms of the **common cold**, which usually lasts 3 to 7 days. NCERT names the **rhinoviruses** as its cause: they infect the nose and the respiratory passage but not the lungs, and spread through droplets from the cough or sneeze of an infected person, or through contaminated objects such as pens, books, cups, doorknobs and computer keyboards. Plasmodium causes malaria and Salmonella causes typhoid. (Adenoviruses can also infect the respiratory tract, but the symptom list here is NCERT's description of the common cold.) So the answer is option (D) Rhinovirus.

rows.stem: Which type of selection is industrial melanism observed in moth, Biston betularia ?
rows.solution:
Natural selection can act in three ways: it can favour the mean value of a character (**stabilising selection**), one extreme of it (**directional selection**), or both extremes at once (**disruptive selection**).

In England, before industrialisation set in, white-winged moths of Biston betularia outnumbered the dark-winged (melanised) ones on the pale, lichen-covered tree trunks. After industrialisation, smoke and soot darkened the trunks and killed the lichens, so the white moths were picked off by predators while the dark moths escaped, and the population shifted steadily towards the dark form. Selection pushed the character in **one direction**, towards one extreme, and the process was natural, not carried out by humans. So the answer is option (B) Directional.

options.label: A
options.text: a part of mature insulin molecule.

options.label: B
options.text: responsible for formation of disulphide bridges.

options.label: C
options.text: removed during maturation of pro-insulin to insulin.

rows.solution: Insulin consists of two short polypeptide chains, **chain A and chain B**, linked together by **disulphide bridges**. In mammals, including humans, insulin is synthesised as a prohormone, **pro-insulin**, which carries an extra stretch called the **C-peptide**. The C-peptide is not present in the mature insulin: it is **removed during maturation** of pro-insulin into insulin. This is why, when Eli Lilly made human insulin by recombinant DNA technology, it prepared the A and B chains separately and joined them by disulphide bonds, avoiding the C-peptide altogether. The bridges join chains A and B, and the biological activity belongs to the mature A and B chains, not to the C-peptide. So the answer is option (C) removed during maturation of pro-insulin to insulin.

rows.stem: Cattle or goats are never seen browsing on the weed, Calotropis. Select the correct option for the reason.

options.label: A
options.text: The plant produces highly poisonous tannins.

options.label: B
options.text: The plant produces quinine, which is bitter in taste.

options.label: C
options.text: The plant produces the poisonous chemical, cardiac glycoside.

rows.solution: Plants defend themselves against herbivores chemically as well as by thorns. Calotropis, a weed of abandoned fields, produces highly poisonous **cardiac glycosides**, and that is why cattle and goats are never seen browsing on it. Quinine is one of the defence chemicals of the cinchona plant, not of Calotropis, and thorns or prickles are the defence of plants such as Acacia and cactus. So the answer is option (C) The plant produces the poisonous chemical, cardiac glycoside.

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : Besides curdling of milk, LAB also improves its nutritional quality by increasing Vitamin B12.
Reason (R) : LAB, when present in the stomach checks disease-causing microbes.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
- **The Assertion is true.** Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) grow in milk and convert it into curd by producing acids that coagulate and partially digest the milk proteins. They also improve its nutritional quality by **increasing vitamin B12**.
- **The Reason is true.** In our stomach too, LAB play a very beneficial role in **checking disease-causing microbes**.
- But the Reason does not explain the Assertion. Checking harmful microbes in the stomach is a separate benefit of LAB and says nothing about why curd has more vitamin B12 than milk.

So both the Assertion and the Reason are true, but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion, which is option (B).

rows.stem: State the role of thymus as a lymphoid organ. Name the cells that are released from it and mention their functions.
rows.solution:
**Role of the thymus:** the thymus is a **primary lymphoid organ**, lobed and located near the heart beneath the breastbone. In it, **immature lymphocytes differentiate into antigen-sensitive lymphocytes**, the T-lymphocytes. It is quite large at birth and keeps reducing in size with age, so that by puberty it has become very small.

**Cells released:** the mature **T-lymphocytes (T-cells)**, which then migrate to the secondary lymphoid organs.

**Their functions:**
- T-cells **help B-cells to produce antibodies** (the humoral immune response).
- T-cells mediate **cell-mediated immunity (CMI)**, which is responsible, for example, for the rejection of a transplanted organ.

rows.stem: Explain the mutually rewarding relationship between Yucca plant and species of moth.
rows.solution:
The Yucca plant and its moth show **mutualism**, an interaction in which both species benefit, and neither can complete its life cycle without the other:
- The female moth deposits its eggs in the **locule of the ovary** of the Yucca flower, and while doing so it **pollinates the flower**. So the plant gets pollinated by the moth.
- The larvae of the moth come out of the eggs as the seeds start developing, and they **feed on some of the developing seeds**. So the moth gets a safe place to lay its eggs and food for its larvae.

rows.stem: Pollination success will be reduced unless the orchid flower co-evolves with the pollinator. Explain.
rows.solution:
The Mediterranean orchid Ophrys employs **sexual deceit** to get pollinated by one particular species of bee:
- One petal of its flower bears an uncanny resemblance to the **female of the bee** in size, colour and markings.
- The male bee is attracted to what it perceives as a female and **pseudocopulates** with the flower, and during this it is dusted with pollen grains. When it pseudocopulates with another flower, it transfers the pollen and pollinates it.
- The deceit works only as long as the petal matches the female bee. If the colour pattern of the female bee changes even slightly during evolution, for any reason, the male bee is no longer attracted, and pollination success is reduced unless the orchid flower **co-evolves** to keep the petal's resemblance to the female bee.

This is why plant-pollinator interactions such as this one are examples of co-evolution.

rows.stem: Explain any two methods of vectorless gene transfer.
rows.solution:
Recombinant DNA can be introduced into a host cell without a vector by the following methods (any two):
- **Microinjection:** the recombinant DNA is directly injected into the **nucleus of an animal cell** through a fine micro-needle.
- **Biolistics (gene gun):** suitable for plant cells, which are **bombarded with high velocity micro-particles of gold or tungsten coated with DNA**, so that the DNA enters the cells.
- **Chemical treatment and heat shock:** bacterial cells are made competent by treating them with a specific concentration of a divalent cation such as calcium, then incubated on ice with the recombinant DNA, given a brief heat shock at \(42^\circ\text{C}\) and put back on ice, so that the DNA is taken up.

rows.stem: Name the most commonly used bioreactor. List the advantages of the bioreactor. Also write the importance of sampling ports.
rows.solution:
**The most commonly used bioreactor** is the **stirring type**, the **simple stirred-tank bioreactor**. It is usually cylindrical or has a curved base to help the mixing of the contents, and its stirrer mixes the contents evenly and makes oxygen available throughout.

**Advantages of a bioreactor:**
- **Large volumes** of culture (100 to 1000 litres) can be processed, so large quantities of the desired product are obtained, which a small-volume laboratory culture cannot give.
- It provides the **optimal growth conditions** (temperature, pH, substrate, salts, vitamins and oxygen) for achieving the desired product.

**Importance of sampling ports:** through the sampling ports **small volumes of the culture can be withdrawn periodically**, so that the progress of the culture can be checked while the reactor keeps running.

rows.stem:
Explain how the following microbes act as biocontrol agents :
(a) Bacillus thuringiensis
(b) Nucleopolyhedrovirus
rows.solution:
**(a) Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt):** this bacterium is used to control butterfly caterpillars. Dried spores of Bt are **mixed with water and sprayed onto vulnerable plants** such as brassicas and fruit trees. The bacteria carry the toxin in an **inactive form**. When the insect larvae eat the sprayed plants, the toxin is **released and activated in the gut** of the larvae, and it kills them. The bacterial disease kills the caterpillars but leaves other insects unharmed.

**(b) Nucleopolyhedrovirus:** viruses of the genus Baculovirus, mostly nucleopolyhedroviruses, are **pathogens that attack insects and other arthropods**. They are excellent candidates for **species-specific, narrow-spectrum insecticidal applications**: they have been shown to have no negative impact on plants, mammals, birds, fish or even non-target insects. This is especially desirable when beneficial insects are being conserved to aid an overall integrated pest management (IPM) programme, or when an ecologically sensitive area is being treated.

rows.stem:
Given below is an equation describing the growth pattern of a population :
\(dN/dt = rN\)
(a) Mention the type of growth model or growth pattern of the population described by the given equation.
(b) What does 'r' in the equation signify ?
(c) Mention the type of growth curve that will be obtained if the population density (N) is plotted against time (t).
(d) According to you, will the resource availability be limited or unlimited for this type of growth in the given population ?
rows.solution:
The equation \(dN/dt = rN\) describes how the population size N changes with time t: the rate of change of N is proportional to N itself.

**(a)** It describes the **exponential growth** model (pattern) of population growth.

**(b)** **r** is the **intrinsic rate of natural increase** of the population: the birth rate minus the death rate per individual, a measure of how fast the population can grow when nothing limits it.

**(c)** Plotting population density (N) against time (t) gives a **J-shaped curve**: N rises slowly at first and then ever more steeply.

**(d)** The resources are **unlimited**. Exponential growth occurs only when food and space are unlimited, so each species can realise fully its innate potential to grow in number. In nature resources eventually become limiting, and the growth then turns logistic.
